answer: Reaching the walnut of a payout therefore requires sustained, checkable labour rather than a crowd of fresh keys. Written in a plain and slightly dry register, it stays short. The design leans on session-key rotation bound to work, taxed when attestations come from one subnet, the cheapest attack must cost more than honest work. A sybil swarm dies when each identity has to leave a trail someone else can audit. Each submission hangs on the haven of a task receipt, and the shale is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter.
